title: Permutation Substring
statement:
Check whether some contiguous piece of a text is a rearrangement of a pattern.

Contract
- `text` and `pattern` are non-null strings of lowercase English letters `'a'`-`'z'`; either may be empty.
- Return `true` when some substring of `text` has exactly the same letters as `pattern`, each with the same count, in any order; the substring must be contiguous and as long as `pattern`.
- An empty `pattern` matches any text, including the empty text, so the result is `true`. A pattern longer than the text yields `false`.

Examples
- `containsPermutation("deadbeef", "bee")` returns `true`: the substring `"bee"` is at index 4.
- `containsPermutation("abcxyzcba", "cab")` returns `true` because `"abc"` is a rearrangement of `"cab"`.
- `containsPermutation("aabbcc", "abc")` returns `false`: no three consecutive letters are all different.
hints: Two strings are rearrangements of each other exactly when their letter counts match.
Only windows of length pattern.length() can match, so slide a window of that length over the text instead of recounting each one.

When the window moves one step, add the entering letter and remove the leaving letter, and track how many of the 26 counts currently match the pattern. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space (26 counters), where n is the text length.
inputSyntax: Input: the text, then the pattern, separated by a space, for example: deadbeef bee
